# Data Processing
```{r cleaning-function, include=FALSE}
# Clean one year of daily air quality measurements.
# file_path: Path to a CSV file; original O3 measurements are in ppm.
# o3_units: Desired O3 units, either "ppm" (default) or "ppb".
# Returns: A tibble with one row per observed date, daily mean
# concentrations for CO, PM2.5 and O3, and their unit labels.
clean_air <- function(file_path, o3_units = "ppm") {

  # Check the requested O3 units
  o3_units <- match.arg(o3_units, c("ppm", "ppb"))

  # Read data and remove exact duplicate rows before changing values
  air <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    rename(
      date = Date,
      co = `Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration`,
      pm25 = `Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration`,
      o3 = `Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration`
    ) %>%
    mutate(date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%Y"))

  # Replace negative measurements with zero before averaging
  for (pollutant in c("co", "pm25", "o3")) {
    air[[pollutant]] <- pmax(air[[pollutant]], 0)
  }

  # Calculate daily averages and retain unit labels
  daily <- air %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(
      co = mean(co, na.rm = TRUE),
      pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
      o3 = mean(o3, na.rm = TRUE),
      units_CO = first(units_CO),
      units_PM = first(units_PM),
      units_O3 = first(units_O3),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(date)

  # Convert O3 from ppm to ppb when requested
  if (o3_units == "ppb") {
    daily$o3 <- daily$o3 * 1000
  }

  # Update the O3 unit label to match the returned values
  daily$units_O3 <- o3_units

  return(daily)
}
```
```{r check-cleaning-function, include=FALSE}
# Use the default O3 units: ppm
daily_2018 <- clean_air("data/AQ_2018.csv")

# Request O3 concentrations in ppb
daily_2018_ppb <- clean_air("data/AQ_2018.csv", o3_units = "ppb")

# Check the number of rows and duplicate dates
nrow(daily_2018)
sum(duplicated(daily_2018$date))

# Check the O3 unit labels
unique(daily_2018$units_O3)
unique(daily_2018_ppb$units_O3)

# Confirm that the ppb values equal the ppm values multiplied by 1000
all.equal(daily_2018_ppb$o3, daily_2018$o3 * 1000)
```

```{r combine-years, include=FALSE}
# Process the remaining two years using the same function
daily_2019 <- clean_air("data/AQ_2019.csv")
daily_2020 <- clean_air("data/AQ_2020.csv")

# Combine the three years and create variables for tables and plots
air_all <- bind_rows(daily_2018, daily_2019, daily_2020) %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    month = factor(
      lubridate::month(date),
      levels = 1:12,
      labels = month.abb
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(date)

# Check the number of days and date range for each year
air_all %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    days = n(),
    first_date = min(date),
    last_date = max(date),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Check for duplicate dates across the combined dataset
sum(duplicated(air_all$date))

# Check for remaining negative concentrations
colSums(air_all[c("co", "pm25", "o3")] < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
```

# Annual Summary Tables
```{r table-2018}
# Summarise the minimum and maximum processed daily concentrations
table_2018 <- tibble(
  Pollutant = c("CO (ppm)", "PM2.5 (ug/m3)", "O3 (ppm)"),
  Minimum = c(
    min(daily_2018$co, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(daily_2018$pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(daily_2018$o3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  Maximum = c(
    max(daily_2018$co, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(daily_2018$pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(daily_2018$o3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

# Display the table with three decimal places
knitr::kable(
  table_2018,
  digits = 3,
  format.args = list(nsmall = 3),
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Table 1. Minimum and maximum daily pollutant concentrations in 2018."
)
```

# Monthly CO and Ozone Concentrations
```{r monthly-co-o3-summary, include=FALSE}
# Reshape CO and O3 into one concentration column
monthly_co_o3 <- air_all %>%
  select(month, co, o3) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, o3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%
  # Pool daily measurements from the same calendar month across years
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    mean_conc = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_conc = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Calculate standard errors and 95% confidence intervals
  mutate(
    se = sd_conc / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean_conc - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean_conc + 1.96 * se
  )

# Inspect January and May as examples
monthly_co_o3 %>%
  filter(month %in% c("Jan", "May"))
```

```{r plot-co-o3, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5.5, out.width="100%", dpi=300}
# Show monthly means and 95% confidence intervals
ggplot(
  monthly_co_o3,
  aes(x = month, y = mean_conc, color = pollutant)
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ pollutant,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = as_labeller(
      c(co = "CO (ppm)", o3 = "O3 (ppm)")
    )
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(co = "#0072B2", o3 = "#D55E00"),
    breaks = c("co", "o3"),
    labels = c("CO", "O3"),
    name = "Pollutant"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly CO and ozone concentrations",
    subtitle = "Daily measurements pooled across available years",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean daily concentration (ppm)",
    caption = paste(
      "Points: monthly means; error bars: 95% confidence intervals.",
      "Jan-Apr: 2018-2020; May-Dec: 2018-2019.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

The two pollutants have different concentration ranges, so I used two panels with separate y-axis scales to make their monthly patterns clearer. Both pollutants are shown in ppm.

# Monthly PM2.5 Concentrations by Year
```{r monthly-pm25-summary, include=FALSE}
# Calculate the monthly mean PM2.5 concentration separately for each year
monthly_pm25 <- air_all %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r plot-pm25, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.0, out.width="100%", dpi=300}
# Compare monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations across years
ggplot(
  monthly_pm25,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = mean_pm25,
    color = factor(year),
    group = year
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "#0072B2",
      "2019" = "#D55E00",
      "2020" = "#009E73"
    ),
    name = "Year"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations by year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean daily PM2.5 concentration (ug/m3)",
    caption = "2020 data are available only for January-April."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```

I used lines and points to show changes in monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations and make comparisons between years easier.

# Interpretation
CO concentrations were higher in winter and lower in summer, while ozone concentrations were higher in late spring and early summer and lower in winter. Monthly mean PM2.5 concentrations were higher in 2018 than in 2019 during June–August and November–December, showing different monthly patterns between the two years. The 2020 data cover only January–April, so its full-year pattern cannot be assessed; in the first figure, January–April use available daily data from all three years, while May–December use only 2018 and 2019.
